evidence.quote: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends Washington criminal and civil law on intimate and sexual images of minors and adults to cover fabricated depictions, including those made by artificial intelligence. Creates a crime and a civil cause of action for disclosing fabricated intimate images without consent. The text states no effective date.
summary.long: HB 1999 (2024) amends Washington's child sexual exploitation provisions (RCW 9.68A), the intimate-image crime (RCW 9A.86.010) and civil remedies (RCW 7.110). 'Digitization' is defined to include artificial intelligence (Sec. 1), and lacking knowledge that an image was digitized is no defense (Sec. 3(7)). Section 7 creates the crime of disclosing fabricated intimate images: knowing disclosure, without consent and with knowledge of likely harm, is a gross misdemeanor on a first offense and a class C felony after a prior conviction. Minors are liable only if they acted intentionally and maliciously. Exemptions cover public-interest disclosures and interactive computer, mobile and network providers acting on content from others. Section 12 creates a civil cause of action for identifiable depicted individuals harmed by intentional disclosure or threatened disclosure without consent; consent to creation alone does not establish consent to disclosure. Section 14 allows a prevailing plaintiff to recover the greater of actual damages or statutory damages up to $10,000 per defendant, plus monetary gain, punitive damages up to three times actual damages, fees and injunctive relief. Section 15 sets a four-year limitation period, tolled for minors until majority. Sections 4 to 6 adjust evidence handling for minor depictions, including fabricated ones.

notes: Bill text as provided; no session law number, effective date or signing date appears in the document. Amends 13 RCW sections and adds new section 7 (crime, chapter 9A.86 RCW) and new section 12 (civil action, chapter 7.110 RCW); the new sections have no RCW numbers in the text, so they are not coded as separate relations. The text does not mark new text by underlining, so the exact changed wording cannot be verified in every amended section. Internal points: 'child' is under 19 in RCW 7.110.010(1), while 'minor' is under 18 in RCW 9.68A.011(5). 'Digitization' is defined in three places (RCW 9.68A.011(8), section 7(6)(a), RCW 7.110.010(4)) with differing wording. RCW 7.110.060 contains struck-through markup '((2))', rendered as plain text. No effective date appears in the text.
